title: fix(core,plugin-view,types): the density fold tests an own key; the flat-property warning and NamedListView's docblock stop naming retired channels (objectui#10868)
body:
Fixes #10868
Clause-②: no

Three hygiene leftovers from the objectui#7924 and objectui#7928 retirements, as the card's Fix section lists them. Claim `5861960491`, seat `domain:ui#1`. The implementing dev ran under session `session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` (the dispatching seat's id).

## What changed

1. **`@object-ui/core`: the density fold tests an own key.** `normalizeListViewSchema` set `foldRowHeight` with `legacyDensity in DENSITY_MODE_TO_ROW_HEIGHT`. It now uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(DENSITY_MODE_TO_ROW_HEIGHT, legacyDensity)`. That is the idiom `rowHeightToDensityMode` and `LIST_VIEW_KINDS` already use in the same file. It was the only `in` operator in that file's code.
2. **`@object-ui/plugin-view`: the dev-mode flat-property warning in `generateViewSchema`.** It said "Move them under options.KIND". It now says "Move them under its top-level KIND block ({ KIND: { ... } })", which is the block `viewOptions[viewType]` reads. A comment above it says why.
   - The edit sits above the VIEW-TYPE BRANCHES `#region`.
   - Nothing inside the HOST-COMPOSITION `#region` changed. objectui#10758 works there.
3. **`@object-ui/types`: `NamedListView`'s docblock.** It said "Used in ObjectViewSchema.listViews for named views".
   - It now says that no member of the contract has been typed by it since objectui#7928.
   - It names the two type pins that hold this in `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.test.ts`: `_ListViewsIsNoLongerTheLocalRecord` and `_ListViewsIsTheSpecRecord`.
   - It says the type stays exported, and that whether it is retired or narrowed follows objectui#7924.
   - The interface is byte-identical.
4. **Changeset** `.changeset/10868-list-view-leftovers.md`: `patch` for `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/types`. `@object-ui/plugin-view` is not listed, because the warning does not ship (measured below).

## Measurements

**The fold, on the built package.** These readings come from `@object-ui/core`'s `dist`, as resolved from `plugin-view`, with `normalizeListViewSchema({ densityMode: X })`:

| X | base `de1b879a6` | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `'toString'`, `'constructor'`, `'hasOwnProperty'`, `'valueOf'` | `rowHeight` is a function, key dropped | `rowHeight` undefined, key kept |
| `'__proto__'` | `rowHeight` is `Object.prototype`, key dropped | `rowHeight` undefined, key kept |
| `'cozy'` (control) | undefined, key kept | undefined, key kept |
| `'compact'` / `'spacious'` | `'compact'` / `'tall'`, key dropped | unchanged |

**The pin is red on base and green on head.** The new cases sit in `normalize-list-view.test.ts` under `densityMode → rowHeight`.
- Each of the five inherited keys stays unfolded, and with `viewType: 'grid'` the input comes back by reference.
- A control case checks that `'cozy'` stays unfolded and `'compact'` still folds.
- I wrote the test before the fix: `Tests 5 failed | 87 passed (92)`. The 5 failures are the inherited keys (`expected [Function toString] to be undefined`), and the control stayed green.
- With the fix: `Tests 92 passed (92)`.

**Where the fold is still reachable.** This answers the card's reachability question.
- The fold runs at three call sites:
  - plugin-list `ListView`, on its own schema;
  - plugin-view `ObjectView`, on the host `views` entry (the `rowHeight` relay, inside the HOST-COMPOSITION fence);
  - app-shell `ObjectView`, on the stored view definition.
- A named view refuses `densityMode` by name: `unrecognized_keys` at `listViews.v1`, for `'compact'` too. The control `rowHeight: 'compact'` is accepted.
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0's `dist` has 0 `densityMode` hits. The control `rowHeight` has 4 hits in `dist/index.js`.
- The `list-view` node's zod schema still declares `densityMode` as a three-value legacy enum. It accepts `'compact'` and refuses `'toString'` with `invalid_value`.
- So a real density still reaches the fold from a `list-view` node, a host `views` entry or a stored view body. `'toString'` reaches it only on a path that does not validate.
- No public door was driven.

**The warning's remedy, run once.** I used a temporary probe (not committed). It renders the real `ObjectView` with a host `views` kanban entry and NODE_ENV stubbed to `development`.
- A flat `groupField: 'stage'` gives lane `status`. The warning now reads "The view uses flat properties ["groupField"]. Move them under its top-level kanban block ({ kanban: { ... } }) …".
- Moved as the new text says, `kanban: { groupField: 'stage' }` gives lane `stage` and no warning.
- Moved as the retired text said, `options: { kanban: { groupField: 'stage' } }` gives lane `status` and no warning. The old text sent the author to a place nothing reads.

**The warning does not ship.** plugin-view's `vite.config.ts` defines `process.env.NODE_ENV` as `"production"`, and the build removes the development branch.
- After `turbo run build`, `Spec Compliance` and `Move them under` have 0 hits in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.umd.cjs`. The control `ObjectView data fetch error` hits both files.
- `files` is `dist`, README, CHANGELOG and LICENSE.
- So plugin-view gets no changeset entry: its CHANGELOG would describe text that no consumer receives. `check-changeset-presence` is satisfied by the one changeset: "4 source file(s) of 3 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)".

**The docblock ships.** In `types/dist/objectql.d.ts`, the old sentence has 0 hits and the new pin name has 1.

## Verification, all at head `96c9f9953`

Heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock.sh`, and each exit was captured with the output redirected first.

- Build: `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/plugin-view...` gave 16 of 16 tasks successful, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0 for each of `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/plugin-view`. I captured each exit on its own, and the script name echoed. core's test program lists the pin file (`--listFiles`).
- `vitest run packages/core/ packages/types/ packages/plugin-view/`: 491 files, 9613 tests passed, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- Downstream consumers of the fold: `packages/plugin-list/` plus the 13 app-shell and react test files that name `densityMode`, `normalizeListViewSchema` or `rowHeight`. 117 files, 1310 tests passed.
- `vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (the whole directory): 177 files passed and 2 skipped (179), 5317 tests passed.
- Gates that exited 0:
  - changeset gates: `check-changeset-presence`, `-no-major`, `-fixed`, `-overwrite` ("1 changeset(s) added, 0 modified"), `-claims`, and `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)") and `check:spec-symbols`;
  - test-harness gates: `check:test-path-roots` and the three `check:vi-mock-*`;
  - reader gates: `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:doc-types`, `check:prompt-keys`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:metadata-write-doors` and `check:registry-bare-names`;
  - coverage and import gates: `check-lint-coverage`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check:self-import` and `check:phantom-deps`;
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the 5 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED:
  - `check:readme-exports`. Prerequisite not met: 20 packages are unbuilt, and its population floor refused the run. No README is touched.
  - `check:sdui-registration-pins`. It needs a console build.
  - Spec Main Shape Gate.
  - CI runs all three.
- ESLint `--no-inline-config --format json` on the 4 touched TS/TSX files: 0 errors and 94 warnings, the same per-file counts as base (60 and 34).
  - Population: all 4 files are in lint scope.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` has 0 `projectService` / `parserOptions` (the control `languageOptions` has 1), so linting is not type-aware.
  - No `eslint-rules/` rule reads the disk, so no untouched file's verdict can move.

## Acceptance notes

- **The warning's per-key remedy.** This predates the PR and is not changed here. Moving a flat key into the named block word for word lands on a spelling the branch strips, for `groupBy` on kanban and `dateField` on calendar.
  - Measured with the same probe: `kanban: { groupBy: 'stage' }` gives lane `status` and no warning, while the control `groupByField` gives `stage`.
  - `calendar: { dateField: 'due' }` gives a node without `startDateField` and no warning, while the control `startDateField` gives `due`.
  - The retired text had the same word-for-word shape. The text is development-only and does not ship, so no card is filed. `.changeset/10002-map-style-remedy-text.md` describes how the map warning's remedy was made executable. Carrier: none.
- **Stale prose that names `options.kanban.conditionalFormatting` as the nested home.** It appears in the `generateViewSchema` kanban-branch comment ("nested `options.kanban.conditionalFormatting` wins") and in the header of `ObjectView.kanbanConditionalFormatting.test.tsx`. Since objectui#7928 the nested home is the top-level `kanban` block. These are comments only, so I left them untouched. The file is shared with objectui#10758's claim, so the in-place exemption does not apply. Carrier: none.
- **The comment above `legacyViewOptions`.** It describes `options.KIND` as retired and folded at `ViewPreview`, which is correct, so it is unchanged.
